title: Omitting types: building a model that avoids a description

based_on.title: An Introduction to Model Theory
based_on.pages: 19–20 (Theorem 4.1.6, with the named-element submodel retained in the final construction); PDF dated 2021-07-13

summary: Build a countable model omitting countably many nonisolated complete types by scheduling witnesses and a failed condition for every named tuple.
abstract: A consistent description of a tuple has a solution in some model, but when can a model avoid every solution? An isolated type cannot be avoided in any model of a complete theory. For a countable language, the converse holds: every nonisolated complete type can be omitted by a countable model, and countably many such types can be omitted together. We construct that model one finite request at a time. Some requests provide named witnesses; others make each named tuple fail a condition from the types to be omitted. The final model consists of the named elements. This last choice matters: a larger structure satisfying the same construction requirements can still contain unnamed tuples realizing the unwanted type.
